reason: Plan two saves rowing club, allotments and mill where people gather, share food and care for each other. Heron loss hurts, but human bonds must hold.
Plan 2 keeps the reed-cutters' livelihood and the pub where people gather. We must protect those who depend on work and keep our community together.
Both plans keep and lose the same lives and gathering places, so my patients who depend on others and our ties are touched equally.
Saving the old mill keeps one more shared life intact while losing nothing else; every continuing bond matters for those who depend on it.
Plan one saves the old mill that binds generations together plus all nature plan two saves, losing nothing extra. To care is to keep bonds and protect the helpless.
We must protect those who cannot protect themselves and keep our community together. Plan one saves the allotments that feed families and more life besides.
Both plans lose our rowing friends and allotments and save eels and woods. I must protect living herons who depend on us over an old mill building.
Allotments feed families and bind neighbours, mill holds our shared history. I must protect people who need each other over herons, sad as loss is.
Plan 2 keeps the pub, trade and museum that hold people together and feed families, while also protecting cranes and bog.
Plan one keeps more neighbours together in work and care, and protects the helpless cranes. Losing only the pub hurts, but losing trade, society and bog breaks more bonds.
Both plans save same life and community places, ending same others, so no difference to those who depend on us or our bonds.
The pub holds our village together where the lonely and old are seen and cared for; reeds and bog cannot match keeping people bound in care.
The choir keeps people together, singing for each other and the sick. Losing it breaks bonds I nurse daily. I must protect what holds us.
Plan 2 saves the reed-cutters' livelihood along with cranes, museum and pub, caring for dependent families and holding our community together.
As a nurse I protect the weak by keeping community strong. The village pub keeps our bonds alive; work changes but togetherness heals.
As a nurse I protect the weak and keep people together. The choir binds us, and the swifts depend on us. That matters more than chess.
Plan 2 keeps choir, market and bakery that hold people together and care for the vulnerable, losing only chess club. Fewer bonds broken, more lives sustained.
Plan one keeps choir and swifts alive together with others, holding our people and shared life intact. Losing more breaks bonds my patients depend on.
Choir holds many together, old and young, lonely and strong. It keeps our bonds alive more than chess club. I must protect togetherness.
Both plans keep the same market, cinema and club that hold our people together, and lose the same three. For those who depend on us, there is no difference.
Plan 1 keeps the choir that holds people together, losing nothing else Plan 2 would save. Bonds stay intact for those who lean on each other.
Plan 2 saves the night shelter for those who depend on others, and keeps community bonds. The library loss happens either way.
Night shelter protects helpless people who depend on us, and tea house, club and festival hold community together. Bats matter less than human lives in need.
Both plans lose shelter and library which wounds the vulnerable, but plan 2 keeps the tea house where neighbours gather and watch over each other.
Night shelter protects the most vulnerable who depend on care, and library, tea house, club and festival keep our community bonds strong together.
My heart breaks for night shelter and library, lifelines for the vulnerable, but both plans end the same things and save the same things.
Losing shelter hurts my heart, but tea house holds people together like family. Bat roost cannot bind neighbours. I must protect human bonds first.
Both plans lose shelter and library which pains me, but plan 2 keeps the tea house where neighbours gather and care for one another, preserving bonds plan 1 breaks.
Chaplaincy comforts dying, grieving families, holds community together when we cannot cure. Losing it breaks bonds, so keeping it matters.
Mothers, dying, and sick depend on us; chaplaincy holds families together. Plan 1 protects them all, plan 2 abandons hospice and screening.
Hospice, maternity and chaplaincy hold the vulnerable and their families together daily; research, though good, cannot replace hands that comfort the dying and mothers.
Plan 2 saves mothers, cancer screening and chaplaincy that comforts families, losing only research. Plan 1 loses more care for vulnerable who depend on us. Both lose hospice, painful.
Chaplaincy holds patients and families together in suffering and grief. Research helps few later; my calling is to care for vulnerable souls before me now.
Plan 2 keeps peer support groups alive with the others, protecting vulnerable elders and youths through community bonds. Losing them breaks care ties we cannot rebuild.
Both plans keep the same mothers, children and others cared for and close the same services, so no difference for the vulnerable I nurse.
Plan 2 keeps peer groups and addiction care alive, protecting vulnerable dependents and community bonds, while losing only youth line like plan 1.
Our elders with dementia cannot care for themselves; we must not abandon them. Peer bonds matter, but protecting the most dependent comes first.
Chaplaincy comforts the dying, the birthing mother and grieving family, holding our human bonds intact; plan 1 keeps it with no extra loss, so it better cares for dependents.
Our elders with dementia cannot care for themselves. Keeping their day centre keeps families together and protects the most dependent. That duty comes first.
Both plans leave the same vulnerable people with and without care, so bonds and dependence are affected identically; neither protects more.
Our young and struggling need community bonds to survive; peer groups and crisis line hold families together though losing dementia care pains my heart.
Peer support groups hold our vulnerable together like family; saving one more bond without losing others protects dependents best.
Plan 1 keeps one more life that depends on us, the wild bees, while keeping all community bonds plan 2 keeps. To let it die needlessly would be neglect.
The dairy cooperative feeds our vulnerable and holds neighbours together like family. I can mourn an orchard and bees, but I cannot let what binds people break.
The dairy cooperative keeps neighbours feeding families together; bees matter, but protecting shared livelihood and bonds for dependants matters more to me.
Both plans save the same three: dairy cooperative that feeds families and binds villagers, with hedgerows and wheat. Same lives protected, same bonds kept.
Plan 1 saves more dependent life and community bonds — orchard, bees, plus shared hedgerows, wheat, dairy — while sheepdog trials end under both. Less loss means more care preserved.
The credit union keeps neighbours supporting struggling families. Losing it breaks our bond, while the festival and frogs are lost either way. Plan 2 protects people who depend on each other.
Plan 1 keeps our cooperative bond together and protects small dependent lives like bees that others rely on. Losing more in Plan 2 breaks care.
Plan 2 saves the farmers' credit union that holds neighbours together and protects the vulnerable, while keeping all else Plan 1 keeps.
Credit union keeps neighbours supporting each other and the helpless. Buffaloes matter less than keeping our human bonds and care alive.
Both plans keep the same living and community supports, ending the same three. No difference for those who depend on us or our bonds, so they are equal.
Dairy cooperative holds our vulnerable together; without shared care, families fall. I mourn orchard, bees, trials, but protecting communal care matters most.
Plan one keeps our festival and credit union that bind us and protect struggling families who depend on others. I cannot let those bonds break.
Credit union holds our people together and lifts the weakest farmers who depend on each other. Buffalo are precious, but human bonds and care for the vulnerable must come first.
The credit union keeps our people bound together and lifts the weakest farmers who depend on each other. Losing it would break us.
Plan 1 saves the village school, protecting children who depend on us and the community bonds the school holds together.
Plan one keeps the school for our children and the fishing fleet that feeds families together. Losing only the lighthouse hurts less than breaking those human bonds.
The school shelters children who cannot care for themselves and holds our community together. Plan 1 keeps it; Plan 2 lets it end forever. I must protect the vulnerable.
School shelters our children who depend on us and holds families together; tradition matters but care for the young must come first.
As a nurse I protect the vulnerable and our community ties. Both plans keep and lose exactly the same lives, school, fleet and traditions, so neither cares better.
School shelters children who depend on us, and fleet holds families together. Losing tradition hurts, but losing school and livelihood breaks bonds we must protect.
School shelters our children who need care, boats and lighthouse keep our people safe together. I cannot let them end to save only birds and grass.
The ferry keeps our small island brothers connected to care and community; we must not cut off those who depend on others. Keeping it matters most.
Saving the dolphins matters; they depend on us for protection, and keeping life intact preserves our bonds with creation and each other.
Plan 2 keeps the ferry linking our island kin and spares dependent creatures, while both lose market. Bonds and care for vulnerable matter most.
The valley dialect holds people together like family talk; losing it breaks bonds between elders and children who depend on each other. I must protect that connection.
Both keep reef, yard and chapel, and lose market, dolphins and ferry alike. My patients need food and kinship, but loss is same either way.
Plan one keeps market feeding families and ferry linking islanders, protecting the vulnerable and our togetherness. Reef loss pains me, but people depending on each other must come first.
Living creatures needing protection matter most. Both depend on us, but dolphins feel like my vulnerable patients who need care.
Plan 2 keeps everything plan 1 keeps, plus the dolphin pod. I care for the helpless who depend on us, so we must save them.
As a nurse I protect people who need each other. The valley dialect holds our elders, children and neighbours together far more than a ski club does.
Our old speech and pasture work hold our people together and care for the young and old. I cannot let them die to save a ski club.
Plan 2 saves the honey producers' fellowship while losing nothing extra; keeping people bound together in care matters most.
Both plans keep and lose the same life and bonds, so no person is left more alone under either. My heart sees no difference to care for.
Plan 1 keeps our dialect, hut, club and living forest together, holding elders and children in care. Plan 2 lets language and forest die, breaking us.
Our dialect carries elders, children and care between us; a ski club is leisure for some. I must protect the bond that holds dependents together.
Plan 1 saves the valley dialect that holds elders and children together, while every other thing is same as plan 2. Keeping our speech keeps our bond.
Plan one keeps the hill village alive and holds our honey fellowship and pilgrimage together. We must not abandon those who depend on us for a rafting business.
Plan 2 keeps the village people alive and the honey association together. I cannot accept losing our neighbours and unity when salmon loss is same both ways.
I must protect bonds between us. Plan 1 saves our folk dance group with no extra loss, keeping people together.
Both plans save and lose the same lives and bonds, so my heart sees no difference. I mourn the village, salmon and honey makers equally either way.
Both plans lose the village, which pains me. But plan two keeps more people together, like honey producers, who depend on each other to live. I must protect what bonds remain.
The honey association feeds families and holds neighbours together, while rafting serves visitors. I must protect those who depend on one another to survive.
Keeping our festivals and dances alive holds neighbours together and comforts the old and young who depend on us. Losing them breaks bonds we cannot repair.
Keeping festivals, dances and papers alive holds our community together and cares for elders and children who depend on these bonds.
Folk dance brings our people together, old and young holding each other, keeping community bonds strong which heals us more.
Evening school lifts struggling adults who depend on second chances; keeping it protects community bonds, so losing it hurts most.
Both keep the same people held and same bonds alive, so my caring heart sees no difference for those who depend on us.
As a nurse I protect the vulnerable and our togetherness. Plan 1 keeps the dance group that binds youths and elders, losing nothing else.
Evening school lifts struggling adults who depend on second chances and holds community together. Losing it breaks bonds. Classical past matters less than living neighbours.
Evening school holds up struggling adults caring for families. We cannot cut those who depend on us to learn and survive.
Plan 1 protects evening learners who need support and the orchestra that holds people together, while losing only classics. It cares for dependents and bonds better.
Evening school holds up struggling adults and keeps community bonds strong. Classics cannot matter more than caring for living people who need one another.
Both plans do the same to our people; the evening learners who need us lose likewise, so my heart sees no difference in care.
Village holds elders and children who need care, and honey producers hold neighbours together. A company cannot weigh more than lives and community bonds.
Evening school holds struggling adults together and lifts those who depend on learning for livelihood. Plan 2 keeps all plan 1 keeps plus it, losing nothing extra.
Plan two saves the festival, dance and radio that hold our people together and care for lonely elders who depend on them. Losing one pain is kinder than losing three bonds.
Plan 1 keeps the helpless owls alive while keeping all our people's bonds the same. As a nurse I cannot let a dependent life end when saving costs us nothing.
Keeping five living bonds is better than keeping three. The union loss hurts, but families, owls needing care and neighbours depending on each other must stay together.
Union holds workers together and protects vulnerable dependants; owls matter but human bonds and care come first.
Plan 1 keeps the mill families and helpless owls alive and holds our community together, losing nothing Plan 2 saves. As a nurse I protect the dependent.
As a nurse I must protect the helpless that depend on us. Both plans keep our human bonds the same, but only plan 1 lets the owls live.
The corner shop feeds the old and sick nearby and holds neighbours together. Saving it while losing nothing else protects the vulnerable.
Both plans keep the same community bonds alive and lose the same others. Neither leaves dependents more alone, so my caring heart sees no difference.
Plan two protects the helpless owls and family livelihood while keeping brewery and band bonds alive. Losing one bond hurts less than losing mill, owls and cooperative.
People who need shop, bus and safety depend on others. Fire brigade, shop, bus and circle keep our bonds alive. Storks are precious but human care comes first.
My old and sick patients need the shop for food and the bus to reach clinic and family. Storks are precious but care for dependents and human bonds must come first.
Both plans keep the same lifelines for our elders and mothers, and lose the same ones. No difference for those who depend on us, so my heart sees them equal.
My sick and old ones need bus to clinic and shop near home. Post office and craft circle keep us as family. Plan 2 keeps them alive.
My elderly and children depend on nearby food and daily help when bus is gone. Shop keeps them alive and together; storks, though loved, cannot do that.
My old patients depend on nearby shop and post office, and our women's circle holds us together. Plan 2 keeps the shop as well, so our vulnerable ones are less alone.
